slides.title: 13 days into my second app. here's the {honest} update.
slides.body: what works, what broke, the thing i got wrong, and what's next.

slides.title: from kitverify to {wordburn}.
body: i stopped trying to build something big.
i'm building one small tool i wanted myself: an app that puts captions on your videos, {right on your phone}. nothing gets uploaded. no sign-up.

slides.title: captions, made on your phone.
items: your video never leaves your phone

slides.title: where it stands.
stats: phone it's been tested on. mine.
slides.note: that's honest, not sad. it isn't in the play store yet.

slides.title: it worked. my computer {swore} it didn't.
body: every time i built the app for my phone, the process said "failed". no reason. no message.
the app was actually done and sitting right there. a tiny helper step was quitting a split second early and calling that a failure.
one line to fix. finding it was the hard part.

slides.title: i was charging for the {wrong thing}.
body: free users got 3 saves, then a paywall. but you don't need to save a video to check the captions: the preview is exactly what you'll get.
so the limit was punishing people for finishing.
now: save as many as you like, free, with a small mark in the corner. pay once and it's gone.

slides.title: the parts that don't exist yet.
items: getting it into the google play store. not there yet.
the first person to buy it. nobody has, because nobody can yet.
posting here as each one happens.

slides.title: the wins and the mess, {as they happen}.
body: what do you wish your captions app did? tell me in the comments. i read every one.
